prerequisites.title: Paid Help Scout plan
prerequisites.detail: The Free plan has no API access. Standard excludes reporting endpoints; Plus has all endpoints.

prerequisites.title: Active invited Help Scout user
prerequisites.detail: Credentials must be tied to an active, invited user, or the API returns 401.

steps.title: Create app in Help Scout profile
steps.detail: Go to Your Profile > My apps > Create My App. Enter a redirection URL; for client credentials only, a placeholder is allowed.
steps.done_when: You have an application ID and secret.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Fetch the callback URL from the Composio dashboard and check it matches the app's Redirection URL.
steps.done_when: Redirection URL in My apps equals the Composio URI.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the help_scout auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Connect a test user account
steps.detail: Open the authorization flow and approve as a Help Scout user.

traps.title: The Inbox API 2.0 limits are stated per account
traps.detail: The Inbox API 2.0 limits are stated per account (200 requests/minute, 12 write requests per 5 seconds burst); the page gives no separate lower limit for unreviewed apps.

traps.title: Access tokens expire after 2 days
traps.detail: Plan for token refresh or re-request in your agent.

traps.title: No managed app for prototypes
traps.detail: Unlike Gmail or GitHub, you cannot prototype on a Composio-managed app.

traps.title: Wrong flow for the audience
traps.detail: Client Credentials is meant for internal integrations; use Authorization Code for other users.

The quote states access tokens expire after 2 days.
The quote supports the 200 requests/minute and 12 write requests per 5 seconds limits, but says nothing about the absence of a separate lower limit for unreviewed apps, which is an added claim.

The quotes say the Client Credentials flow is for internal integrations and describe creating an app, but nothing explicitly states that no provider review is needed; this is an inference.
The quotes support creating an app under My apps, but the quotes do not mention requesting a token with client credentials as a step in order; the ordering and token step are only partly supported.
The quote states the Free plan does not include API access, matching the paid-access modifier.
The quote states credentials must be associated with an active, invited user, or a 401 error is returned.
The quotes show the Authorization Code flow is for other users and describe the authorization URL, but nothing states that no provider review is needed.
The quotes support the authorization URL and that users authorize via the authorization screen, but do not explicitly mention creating an app with a redirect URL as a prior step.

The quotes cover plan access restrictions (Free plan excluded, Standard lacks reporting, Plus has all endpoints), but do not state that customers' plans must include API access as a general requirement for this flow.
The quote says brand guidelines should be read before launching, but does not specifically limit the restriction to public-facing projects; the scope is generalised.
The quote states credentials must belong to an active, invited user, with a 401 error otherwise.

The quotes support self-serve app creation and that the Authorization Code flow is typical for multi-user integrations, but nothing documents the roughly one-hour time, the absence of review, or that the main cost is a paid plan.
